GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The min-twin scheme predates this repository: static/ was copied 1:1 from mark-electron@v1.2.3 on 2026-04-28 (commit 02cb6a9f, whose body names the copy), and upstream marktext commits no twins at all — its minification scheme is the uncommitted build-time scripts/minify-locales.ts, exactly the generate-at-build alternative the owner rejected (checked on GitHub 2026-10-28) — so the twins are a fork-local artifact of an Electron-era loading path. In that path the renderer fetched /locales/<code>.min.json over the Electron static server, where a byte-compacted table measurably reduced wire bytes and parse time; the full table stayed for human editing. The Tauri port broke that path (the fetch 404'd in every build) and replaced it on 2026-10-14 with import.meta.glob lazy chunks inside the renderer bundle (V-M-055 scenario-1), after which the compaction buys nothing measurable: one locale chunk loads once per session and exceeds its twin by 12,818-13,032 bytes as a full table (English is already statically imported in full). Meanwhile the byte-parity law (tests/renderer/i18n/locale-keys.test.js, added 2026-10-27, plus a second value-level sync law in tests/renderer/components/updateNotice.test.js) turns every translated-string edit into a rewrite of ten single-line 49-76 KB files, which is why commit c65c534a carries a 1,131,587-byte locale diff for a 13,128-byte semantic edit (the twins alone: 1,118,459 bytes; git diff counts) and the owner's agent push budgets keep tripping (owner report 2026-10-28: two commits, each rewriting all 20 locale files, over 2 MB combined). The manual regeneration step also already leaks into test hygiene: tests/e2e/settings-tabs-content.spec.ts left a scan degraded "until the .min.json regeneration runs". Removing the twins removes the category of work, not just its cost. The retired parity tests are replaced by an inverted guard (exactly ten full tables, no *.min.json) so the duplicate cannot silently return.

Alternatives.Alternative: Generate twins at build time, keep them out of git: a vite plugin or prebuild script would compact the full tables on every build and test run. Rejected by the owner on 2026-10-28: it preserves the same git-level win but adds a mandatory moving part to dev, test, e2e and CI flows — exactly the kind of forget-to-run step that already produced the degraded e2e scan above — while the runtime benefit it protects is 12.8-13 KB once per session.

Keep twins, stop tracking their churn (LFS, .gitattributes diff suppression): attacks the symptom (diff size) but keeps the parity law, the manual regeneration step, the dead-code false lead and 560,622 bytes of duplicates; also makes locale diffs less reviewable on diff-hungry tooling. Rejected.
Do nothing: the pain is real and recurring (two push-budget incidents on 2026-10-27/28 alone) and grows with every locale-touching feature; rejected by the owner ("this already hurts", 2026-10-28).

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Whether src/common/ as a directory retains any other orphaned marktext modules is a separate hygiene sweep; this change deletes only the verified-dead common/i18n.js.
Whether the ten locale tables should eventually split per-namespace is a future i18n ergonomics question, explicitly out of scope here.

Scenarios.Scenario: Diff math (why 20 files became 2 MB): a .min.json twin is one physical line; a git unified diff replaces whole lines, so one changed key rewrites the entire 49-76 KB line per language — plus its counterpart in the new file. Ten languages therefore contribute ~10 times two line-payloads of pure re-serialization noise per commit, while the ten full tables contribute the same edit as ~21 tidy lines each.

Reader inventory method: repo-wide grep for the literal ".min.json" on 2026-10-28, node_modules and build output excluded, cross-checked against import graphs; the only runtime consumer is localeLoader.js:21 (import.meta.glob), the only disk consumer is the dead src/common/i18n.js (zero importers), the remaining hits are test readers, the two release tools and comments/shim docs.

Bundle impact: vite inlines each full table into its lazy chunk as a JSON module; the chunk grows by the compaction delta (12,818-13,032 bytes per locale, nine lazy chunks — English is already the statically imported full table). No Tauri config ships static/ as files (bundle.resources absent; vite publicDir points at src/renderer/public), so today's installed locale payload is the ten twin chunks (560,622 bytes) plus the static full English table (62,705 bytes) = 623,327 bytes; after the switch it is 689,495 bytes — a 66,168-byte installed growth against a 560,622-byte git-footprint reduction.

C-1.Name: A twin comes back from the dead
C-1.Expected: Any process that recreates static/locales/<code>.min.json (old habit, stale script, cherry-pick from history) fails CI: the locale-keys guard names the offending file; the .gitignore pattern keeps an untracked twin out of the index; AC "exactly ten .json files" is the machine check.

C-2.Name: A reader survives the inventory
C-2.Expected: The plan re-runs the repo-wide grep for "min.json" in both dotted and bare forms after the code lands (node_modules, build output and .grace/changes/** excluded); any hit outside the guard test, the .gitignore entry, frozen history (docs/*.xml provenance) and the updated governance artifacts is a defect; the grep classification in R-3 is an inventory, not a completeness proof — the re-run is.

C-3.Name: Ten languages, identical behaviour
C-3.Expected: BUNDLED_LOCALES resolves the same ten codes from the full tables; switching UI language at runtime loads the identical translation objects (same keys, same values, same ordering) as the twins shipped, because the twins were byte-compactions of exactly these files; English's static import path is untouched.

C-4.Name: The fallbacks still guard the edges
C-4.Expected: An unknown locale code resolves to {} with the [i18n][loadLocaleTable][BLOCK_LOCALE_MISSING] warning; a corrupted table chunk resolves to {} with [i18n][loadLocaleTable][BLOCK_LOCALE_LOAD_FAILED]; systemLocale's resolveSystemLocale (exact, zh script/region, primary subtag, 'en') keeps mapping onto the same ten shipped codes.

C-5.Name: Bundle shape holds
C-5.Expected: The glob switch yields exactly ten lazy locale chunks plus the unchanged static English import (itself already the full table); nothing eagerly imports all ten tables; nine lazy chunks grow by 12,818-13,032 bytes each and gzip narrows that further; no new dependency enters package.json.

C-6.Name: Packaged builds keep their languages
C-6.Expected: Desktop and MAS packaged builds render every UI language (the 2026-10-14 regression class — fetch-era non-English builds silently stayed English — must not return); the installed locale payload grows by a bounded 66,168 bytes while the git footprint shrinks by 560,622 bytes; no packaging manifest changes because none ships static/ as files (bundle.resources absent).

C-7.Name: Release tooling loses the twin, keeps the law
C-7.Expected: A release-normalize dry run over its fixture emits full-table locale changes and no minPath entries, still performing the version-draft rename inside the tables; release-materials validates locale materials against the full tables alone; both tools' suites run green on the twin-free fixture shape in the same bundle.

C-8.Name: Parallel sessions do not eat each other
C-8.Expected: The shared-worktree rule applies: grace lint --parallel-preflight re-run before the first write, not trusted from an earlier run; the graph/verification edits, the guard test, the deletions and the loader switch ship as one bundle so a merging neighbour never sees a half-switched state (loader on twins, twins deleted).

C-9.Name: Dead-code deletion breaks nothing
C-9.Expected: src/common/i18n.js deletion is proven safe by evidence, not assumption: zero importers re-verified immediately before the delete; the exported names (getTranslation, loadTranslations, getAllTranslations, clearCache, isLanguageSupported, getSupportedLanguages) are checked path-scoped — the renderer's window.i18nUtils.loadTranslations is a different symbol that must NOT be flagged — and typecheck:ipc stays clean after removal.

C-10.Name: No residue teaches the old ritual
C-10.Expected: Living documentation (CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/engineering-protocol.md, docs/release-process.md, .grace/context/*.xml including deployment.xml's "Regen *.min.json" step, and code comments in touched files) no longer instructs anyone to read or regenerate twins; frozen history keeps its wording by protocol (docs/*.xml provenance such as development-plan.xml, archive bundles); the guard test is the one deliberate, self-describing exception.

C-11.Name: A fresh clone is complete
C-11.Expected: A clean checkout contains exactly the ten full tables and passes the entire suite with no generation step — the "until the .min.json regeneration runs" class of broken state becomes unreachable; CI on a fresh runner proves it on every push.
